back: A characteristic controlled by a gene on a sex chromosome, so it is more common in one sex.

front: What is a **carrier** of a sex-linked condition?
back: A heterozygous female ($\text{X}^\text{B}\text{X}^\text{b}$) who does not show the condition but can pass the allele on.

front: Where is the gene for red-green colour vision?
back: On the X chromosome. The Y chromosome carries no allele of it.

front: Why is colour blindness more common in males?
back: Males have one X and no allele on the Y, so one recessive allele is expressed; females need two.

front: Where does a son get his X chromosome?
back: Always from his mother (his Y comes from his father).
notes: So a father cannot pass an X-linked allele to his son.

front: What does a father pass to every daughter?
back: His only X chromosome, so all daughters of a colour-blind man are at least carriers.

front: Carrier mother × father with normal vision gives...?
back: Daughters: half normal, half carriers, none colour-blind. Sons: half colour-blind.
notes: Probability a child is colour-blind: 1/4; that a son is: 1/2.
